paper_summary: Six metal matrix syntactic foams (MMSFs) made by pressure infiltration of ~64 vol% ceramic hollow microspheres (E-spheres SL150 / SLG / SL300, mean diameters 100 / 130 / 150 um) with Al99.5 or AlSi12 aluminium matrices were characterised by three hardness methods: global (Brinell) hardness, quasi-static depth sensing hardness and dynamic (Equotip) hardness. Global hardness rose above the matrix value for Al99.5 foams and fell below it for AlSi12 foams, and was nearly matrix-independent, so it is a structural property; the smallest spheres (SL150) always gave the highest global and dynamic hardness. Depth sensing tests revealed the 4Al+3SiO2 -> 2Al2O3+3Si exchange reaction that degrades the microsphere walls in Al99.5 foams, absorbed energy was mostly plastic and varied linearly with the loading slope, and cross-sections showed damage localised directly under the imprints.

structure.microstructure_notes: Pressure-infiltrated block, as-fabricated. Reported porosities (image analysis, Table 2): total 44.67%, 'planned' (hollow-microsphere) 50.86%, 'unwanted' -6.18%. Microspheres are E-spheres (Envirospheres Pty. Ltd.), specific surface 0.06 1/um, composition 30-35% Al2O3, 45-50% amorphous SiO2, 19% mullite, 1% quartz, bal. other. Originally broken spheres removed by a buoyant method. matrix_porosity_fraction left null because the reported unwanted porosity is negative (-6.18%): the authors state the infiltration pressure broke some microspheres and their interiors were infiltrated, so the image-analysis value is not a physical void fraction. Exchange reaction 4Al(liq)+3SiO2(sol) -> 2Al2O3(sol)+3Si(sol) degraded the microsphere walls in the Al99.5 matrix foams (strongest for SL150 and SLG).

test.standard: EN ISO 6506:2005 (Brinell global hardness); ASTM 956-96 (Equotip dynamic hardness); depth sensing hardness test is not standardised
test.specimen_notes: Three hardness tests on each block, 10 measurements each: (1) global Brinell hardness, 10 mm hard steel ball, 1839 N (187.5 kp) for Al99.5 foams and 2452 N (250 kp) for AlSi12 foams, 10 s dwell, imprints ~0.2 mm deep; (2) quasi-static depth sensing hardness on an MTS 810, 2.5 mm hemispherical mandrel to 1600 N at 0.02 mm/s, imprints ~0.4 mm deep with a ~0.5 mm affected zone; (3) dynamic hardness with an Equotip device, 5 g indenter, HD = 1000*va/vb HL. Block size 35 x 55 x 170 mm.

evidence.quote: Tab. 2. The average porosity values of the produced MMSF blocks | Al99.5-SL150 | 44.67 | 50.86 | -6.18

Tab. 1. Geometrical dimensions and phase composition (wt%) of the hollow ceramic spheres [32] | SL150 | average diameter 100 um | specific surface 0.06 um-1 | Al2O3 30-35% | Amorphous SiO2 45-50% | Mullite 19% | Quartz 1% | Bal. Other
The microspheres were compacted by gently tapping. By this way ~64 vol% of microspheres can be incorporated.

When the matrix reached the infiltration temperature (600 C and 710 C in the case of AlSi12 and Al99.5 matrix respectively), Ar gas was let to flow into the chamber with a previously sat infiltrating pressure (0.4 MPa ~ 4 bar). The pressure was maintained for 30 s.

extraction_notes: All hardness results (Fig. 3 global hardness, Figs. 6 and 7 absorbed elastic/plastic/total energies, Fig. 10 dynamic hardness) are plotted only - no numerical hardness or energy values appear in the text or tables - so no property values could be extracted without reading them off the plots, which the prompt forbids. Additionally, the schema has no hardness field (Brinell HBS, depth sensing, Leeb HL) and no field for indentation absorbed energy in J, so even tabulated values could not have been stored in Properties. The extractable quantitative data are therefore composition, processing and structure: microsphere grade, mean diameter and specific surface (Table 1), porosities (Table 2), ~64 vol% microsphere loading, infiltration temperature (600 C for AlSi12, 710 C for Al99.5) and pressure (0.4 MPa for 30 s). One record per produced block type (6 blocks) rather than per hardness method, because no measured value distinguishes the three test conditions; test_type is 'other' since hardness/indentation is not in the TestType enum. particle_volume_fraction 0.64 is the authors' stated packing of the microsphere bed, not a per-block measurement; note that Table 2 lists a 'planned porosity' of 48-51% which is the internal void volume of those spheres, not the sphere volume fraction. For the Al99.5 blocks the reported 'unwanted' porosity is negative (-5.80 to -7.19%) because infiltration broke and filled some microspheres, so matrix_porosity_fraction was left null there and the value recorded in microstructure_notes; the AlSi12 blocks use the reported positive values (1.13-2.03%). Only relative statements are given for hardness (matrices differ by ~40 HBS globally and ~30% dynamically, the latter dropping to ~15% for the foams; AlSi12 foams absorbed ~2.5x more indentation energy than the pure matrix), so these are left in the summary.
